meta.title: Best Phone Under ₹40,000 in India (2026): 6 Phones That Rival the Flagships
meta.description: Ranked: the 6 best phones under ₹40,000 in India for 2026. Real cameras, AMOLED, 5G and battery compared across OnePlus, Samsung, iQOO, Pixel and more.
meta.short_desc: Six near-flagship phones under ₹40,000 -- and one to skip.

headings.text: What actually matters in a phone under ₹40,000
Our picks: 6 phones that rival the flagships

cta.headline: Comparing 30+ phones by budget?
cta.sub: Get our comparison sheet with chipset, charging, IP rating and tested camera samples across every phone we reviewed.

faq.q: Is a ₹40,000 phone better than a ₹25,000 phone in 2026?
faq.a: :For most buyers -- not by much. The ₹25,000 segment already gives you AMOLED 120Hz, 5G and a competent camera. The ₹40,000 segment adds telephoto cameras, faster Snapdragon 8-series chipsets, longer software support and IP ratings. If your current phone is two years old and you take a lot of zoom shots, the upgrade is worth it. Otherwise, save the ₹15,000 and grab a ₹25,000 phone.

faq.q: Which chipset should I look for under ₹40,000?
faq.a: :Snapdragon 8s Gen 3, Snapdragon 8 Gen 2, or Dimensity 9200+. Anything older (Snapdragon 7-series, Dimensity 8000-series) feels sluggish by 2027 standards. The OnePlus 13R (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3), iQOO Neo 9 Pro (Dimensity 9300) and Realme GT 6 (Snapdragon 8s Gen 3) are the chipset winners in this bracket.

faq.q: How important is a telephoto lens under ₹40,000?
faq.a: :Important if you take zoom shots at concerts, weddings or while travelling. Phones with a dedicated 3x telephoto (OnePlus 13R, Vivo V30 Pro) produce dramatically better 3x-10x zoom than phones that crop from the main sensor. For everyday shots under 2x, the main camera is plenty.

faq.q: Should I buy the Pixel 8a or wait for the Pixel 9a?
faq.a: :Buy the Pixel 8a now. It already has Tensor G3, 7 years of OS support (until 2031), and IP67 water resistance at ₹37,999. The Pixel 9a may launch in October 2026 with marginal upgrades but at a ₹45,000+ price. The 8a hits the sweet spot for stock Android.

faq.q: Which phone under ₹40,000 has the cleanest software?
faq.a: :Pixel 8a (stock Android, 7 years of updates), OnePlus 13R (OxygenOS, 4 years of updates), and Samsung Galaxy S23 FE (One UI, 5 years of updates). Avoid Realme UI, FunTouch OS and HyperOS in this bracket if software longevity matters to you.

meta.tldr_pick: Our top pick is the OnePlus 13R. Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 chipset, 6.78-inch 1.5K AMOLED at 120Hz, 50 MP main + 50 MP 2x telephoto, 100W SuperVOOC charging and 5500 mAh battery. At ₹39,999, it is the most balanced near-flagship you can buy in India right now.
key_takeaways: Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 is the floor in 2026: skip any ₹40k phone that ships with Snapdragon 7-series or Dimensity 8000.
Telephoto cameras are worth the ₹10k premium over ₹30k: 3x optical zoom is the single biggest upgrade you get in this bracket.
Software support matters: Pixel 8a gives 7 years, Samsung gives 5, OnePlus gives 4. Realme and Xiaomi give 2-3.
Skip the Nothing Phone (3): ₹37,999 for a phone with a mid-range chipset and no telephoto -- better options exist.
meta.who_for: Anyone buying a phone between ₹30,000 and ₹40,000 in 2026 -- buyers who want near-flagship cameras and chipsets without paying ₹65,000+, professionals who need long software support, mobile photographers who want telephoto lenses, and gamers who want sustained peak performance.
meta.methodology: We compared 11 phones priced ₹29,999 to ₹39,999 on Amazon India and Flipkart in September 2026. For each we evaluated chipset performance (sustained-throttling tests, not just peak AnTuTu), display calibration (peak nits, PWM dimming, colour accuracy), camera sample shots at 1x/3x/10x zoom across daylight and low light, IP rating, charging speed with bundled charger, and manufacturer software support commitment. Picks cross-checked against GSMArena spec sheets, Indian YouTuber reviews and verified buyer feedback.

body:
What actually matters in a phone under ₹40,000

Three years ago, ₹40,000 bought you last year's flagship. In 2026, it buys a phone that is barely distinguishable from ₹65,000+ flagships -- Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 chipset, dedicated telephoto lenses, 100W+ charging and 5+ years of software support. The catch: every phone in this bracket looks great on paper, but only a handful actually deliver on the marketing.

We picked six that do. Here's what we looked at, and which popular model we recommend skipping.

The five specs that decide if a ₹40,000 phone is worth the premium over a ₹25,000 phone: Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 or Dimensity 9200+ chipset, dedicated telephoto lens with 2x or 3x optical zoom, IP67 or IP68 water resistance, 100W+ bundled charger, and 5+ years of OS updates from the manufacturer. AMOLED 120Hz is standard in this segment.

If you only buy one thing from this list: get the OnePlus 13R. Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, 50 MP main + 50 MP 2x telephoto, 100W charging and 5500 mAh battery. At ₹39,999, it is the most balanced near-flagship under ₹40,000 in India right now.

Our picks: 6 phones that rival the flagships

⭐ Top Pick

1. OnePlus 13R

₹39,999
ChipsetSnapdragon 8 Gen 3
Main + Tele50 MP + 50 MP 2x
Display1.5K AMOLED 120Hz
Charging100W SuperVOOC
Battery5500 mAh

OnePlus's 13R packs the same Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 chipset as the flagship OnePlus 13, but at ₹40,000 less. The 50 MP main camera is solid, the 50 MP 2x telephoto is genuinely useful for portraits, and 100W charging takes it from 0 to 100% in 28 minutes. OxygenOS is clean and gets 4 years of updates.

Pros

  • Flagship Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 chipset
  • 100W charging with bundled charger
  • Dedicated 2x telephoto lens
  • OxygenOS is clean and gets 4 years of updates

Cons

  • No wireless charging
  • No IP68 (IP64 splash-resistant only)
  • Camera is good, not flagship-grade
🔥 Performance Pick

2. iQOO Neo 9 Pro

₹35,999
ChipsetDimensity 9300
Main + Tele50 MP + no tele
Display1.5K AMOLED 144Hz
Charging120W FlashCharge
Battery5160 mAh

The Dimensity 9300 inside the iQOO Neo 9 Pro trades blows with the Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 in sustained gaming loads -- the chip throttles less than the SD 8 Gen 2 phones in this bracket. 144Hz display is smoother than 120Hz for games that support it. The camera lacks a telephoto but the main 50 MP Sony IMX920 sensor is excellent.

Pros

  • Dimensity 9300 is a sustained-performance beast
  • 120W charging -- 0 to 80% in 19 minutes
  • 144Hz display great for gaming
  • ₹4,000 cheaper than the OnePlus 13R

Cons

  • No telephoto lens
  • FunTouch OS has ads (can be disabled)
  • Only 3 years of OS updates
📷 Camera Pick

3. Pixel 8a

₹37,999
ChipsetTensor G3
Main + Tele64 MP + no tele
DisplayFHD+ OLED 120Hz
Charging18W
Battery4492 mAh

Google's Pixel 8a is the cleanest Android experience in this bracket. Tensor G3 is tuned for Google's AI features (Magic Editor, Best Take, Audio Magic Eraser) and the phone gets 7 years of OS updates -- until 2031. Camera quality is genuinely flagship-grade thanks to Google's computational photography.

Pros

  • 7 years of Android updates (until 2031)
  • Best-in-class computational photography
  • Stock Android, no bloat
  • IP67 water resistance

Cons

  • 18W charging is painfully slow
  • Tensor G3 is weaker than SD 8 Gen 2 in raw performance
  • Small 4492 mAh battery
  • No telephoto lens
💰 Best Value

4. Realme GT 6

₹34,999
ChipsetSnapdragon 8s Gen 3
Main + Tele50 MP LYT-808 + no tele
Display1.5K AMOLED 120Hz
Charging120W SuperVOOC
Battery5500 mAh

The Realme GT 6 is the cheapest Snapdragon 8s Gen 3 phone in India. The 50 MP Sony LYT-808 main sensor is genuinely impressive for stills, and 120W charging means 0 to 100% in 26 minutes. Realme UI 5 has bloat but the underlying hardware is solid.

Pros

  • Snapdragon 8s Gen 3 at ₹34,999 -- cheapest in segment
  • 120W charging with bundled charger
  • Sony LYT-808 main sensor is flagship-grade
  • 5500 mAh battery

Cons

  • Realme UI 5 has ads and bloat
  • Only 2 years of OS updates promised
  • No IP rating (splash-resistant only)
📸 Telephoto Pick

5. Samsung Galaxy S23 FE

₹39,999
ChipsetSnapdragon 8 Gen 1
Main + Tele50 MP + 8 MP 3x
DisplayFHD+ AMOLED 120Hz
Charging25W
Battery4500 mAh

Samsung's Fan Edition of the S23 is the only phone under ₹40,000 with a 3x optical telephoto. One UI is the most polished Android skin and Samsung promises 5 years of OS updates (until 2028). The Snapdragon 8 Gen 1 is older but still capable for daily use and gaming.

Pros

  • Dedicated 3x optical telephoto
  • 5 years of OS updates
  • IP68 water resistance
  • Wireless charging support

Cons

  • Snapdragon 8 Gen 1 is two generations old
  • 25W charging is slow
  • Smaller 4500 mAh battery
  • Heavier than competitors (209g)
🎮 Camera Phone

6. Vivo V30 Pro

₹39,999
ChipsetDimensity 8200
Main + Tele50 MP + 50 MP 2x
Display1.5K AMOLED 120Hz
Charging80W FlashCharge
Battery5000 mAh

The Vivo V30 Pro is the slimmest phone on this list (7.5 mm) and the only one with Zeiss optics on the main camera. The 50 MP + 50 MP 2x telephoto setup is genuinely capable, and 80W charging refills the battery in 35 minutes. Aura Light flash is a unique feature for portraits in low light.

Pros

  • Zeiss optics on the main camera
  • Slim 7.5 mm design
  • 80W charging is fast
  • Aura Light ring flash for portraits

Cons

  • Dimensity 8200 is mid-range
  • Only 3 years of updates
  • FunTouch OS has bloat

The one we recommend skipping

⛔ Skip This

Nothing Phone (3) -- ₹37,999

ChipsetSnapdragon 7s Gen 2
Main + Tele50 MP, no tele
DisplayFHD+ AMOLED 120Hz
Charging45W
Battery5000 mAh

The Nothing Phone (3) is a beautiful phone with the signature Glyph interface, but at ₹37,999 you are paying ₹10,000 more than the Realme GT 6 for a chipset that is half as fast. The Snapdragon 7s Gen 2 throttles heavily under sustained gaming, the camera lacks a telephoto, and NothingOS still has rough edges in 2026. Skip this and grab the Realme GT 6 or iQOO Neo 9 Pro instead.

Frequently asked questions

Is a ₹40,000 phone better than a ₹25,000 phone in 2026?

For most buyers -- not by much. The ₹25,000 segment already gives you AMOLED 120Hz, 5G and a competent camera. The ₹40,000 segment adds telephoto cameras, faster Snapdragon 8-series chipsets, longer software support and IP ratings. If your current phone is two years old and you take a lot of zoom shots, the upgrade is worth it. Otherwise, save the ₹15,000 and grab a ₹25,000 phone.

Which chipset should I look for under ₹40,000?

Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, Snapdragon 8s Gen 3, or Dimensity 9200+. Anything older (Snapdragon 7-series, Dimensity 8000-series) feels sluggish by 2027 standards. The OnePlus 13R (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3), iQOO Neo 9 Pro (Dimensity 9300) and Realme GT 6 (Snapdragon 8s Gen 3) are the chipset winners in this bracket.

How important is a telephoto lens under ₹40,000?

Important if you take zoom shots at concerts, weddings or while travelling. Phones with a dedicated 3x telephoto (OnePlus 13R 2x, Vivo V30 Pro 2x, Samsung S23 FE 3x) produce dramatically better 3x-10x zoom than phones that crop from the main sensor. For everyday shots under 2x, the main camera is plenty.

Should I buy the Pixel 8a or wait for the Pixel 9a?

Buy the Pixel 8a now. It already has Tensor G3, 7 years of OS support (until 2031), and IP67 water resistance at ₹37,999. The Pixel 9a may launch in October 2026 with marginal upgrades but at a ₹45,000+ price. The 8a hits the sweet spot for stock Android.

Which phone under ₹40,000 has the cleanest software?

Pixel 8a (stock Android, 7 years of updates), OnePlus 13R (OxygenOS, 4 years of updates), and Samsung Galaxy S23 FE (One UI, 5 years of updates). Avoid Realme UI, FunTouch OS and HyperOS in this bracket if software longevity matters to you.

The bottom line

If you want the most balanced phone under ₹40,000 in India, the OnePlus 13R at ₹39,999 is the right pick -- Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, telephoto camera, 100W charging and 4 years of updates. If you want sustained gaming performance, the iQOO Neo 9 Pro at ₹35,999 is faster. If software longevity matters more than raw performance, the Pixel 8a at ₹37,999 is unbeatable with 7 years of updates. If camera quality is your priority, the Vivo V30 Pro or Samsung Galaxy S23 FE deliver telephoto shots you cannot get elsewhere in this bracket.

Avoid the Nothing Phone (3) at this price -- the Snapdragon 7s Gen 2 is the wrong chipset for a ₹38,000 phone in 2026.
